data.body:
**eb58 IS CLOSED — 11 tickets now closed.** The two-provider evidence satisfied its [operator-attested] criterion. Closed: 7761, 172e, 343b, 7cbe, b00f, d8ef, b300, b5fe, d23e, epic 9227, eb58.

THE TWO-PROVIDER RUN, and why it is real evidence rather than a box tick. Config via cb6f's REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE pointer (so the checkout was never edited): frontier=anthropic:claude-opus-4-8, standard=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6, trivial=bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-...
From the 42 per-call `rebar.llm.structured_run` usage lines: **41 calls anthropic:claude-opus-4-8 (96,055 input tokens) and 1 call bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 (2,857 tokens)**. That 41/1 split is EXACTLY the split 3768 documents for the Anthropic-only path — but with Pass-1 on Anthropic and the verifier downgrade on BEDROCK. The per-pass class split survives a provider boundary, which is the capability the epic exists for. provider_provenance recorded provider=bedrock and prompt_cache_style="bedrock" (not "anthropic"), so the capability record is live, not defaulted.
I CORRECTED MY OWN OVER-COUNT before attesting: a whole-log grep for `bedrock:<model>` said 4 calls; three of those were verdict-JSON fields. The real count from lines carrying BOTH `model=` and `input_tokens=` is 1. The attestation says 1 and states the limitation (one Bedrock call proves dispatch, not stability).

TWO PARITY FINDINGS banked for S6/S9: (1) Bedrock REFUSES `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` on-demand — ValidationException demanding an inference profile; `us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` works (verified with an 8-token converse BEFORE the 31-minute gate run). (2) Prompt caching had NO effect on the Bedrock call (cache_read=0/cache_write=0 at 2857 input tokens).

**THE DEPENDENCY ORDER IN MY BRIEF WAS BACKWARDS — corrected from the precheck, which names blockers for free.** The brief said eb58 -> 0d76/eb6e/8625 -> 3768. The truth: **3768 blocks 0d76; 3768+0d76 block eb6e; eb6e blocks 8625.** So the order is 3768 -> 0d76 -> eb6e -> 8625 -> 5e75 -> epic 061c. 3768 is the critical path, not a late follow-up. Also confirmed 1903, a574 and 2932 are already CLOSED, so they are no longer blockers as older notes suggest.

3768 ROUND 1 = BLOCK, 3 findings, all rooted in the plan predating eb58's delivery. Remediated, round 2 running. Notably B1 EXPOSED AN ERROR I HAD INTRODUCED MYSELF in an earlier pre-remediation: I wrote "the gate has THREE prompt steps, not four" — wrong, because I counted only single-shot prompt steps and MISSED THE TWO BATCH STEPS. code-review.yaml has FIVE LLM-calling steps (base :67, round_a :77, round_b :109, verify :143, coach :182); only verify declares model: standard. So FOUR remain unclassed, and my "correction" from four to three made the plan worse and would have shipped two batch steps silently unclassed.
AND I REFUSED ONE THIRD OF A FINDING: B3 bundled three staleness claims, but one is TRUE — review_kernel/verify.py:263-269 `resolve_verifier_model` still reads `verifier_default if model == default_model else ...`, so the equality test IS operative. I fixed the two genuinely stale claims and DEFENDED the true one in the plan text so a later round cannot 'correct' it away. Accepting a finding wholesale would have introduced a fresh error.

PROCESS FAILURES THIS FIRING: (1) I bundled an edit with a review launch in ONE call; the edit FAILED with `flock: could not acquire lock after 60s` (eb58's close held the store lock) and the review launched anyway against un-clarified text. Killed it, waited for the lock, applied the edit, verified it, THEN launched. Do not bundle. (2) I used a shell `&` for that launch instead of run_in_background — no notification. (3) Two content-match failures in a row because a literal spanned a line break ("shipped\n      YAML"); minimal anchors + re.S fixed it. Same whitespace trap as before.
